_comment: Single source of truth for the calculator targets. Type IDs come from the TI link protocol guide / tilibs: TI-83+ PRGM 0x05 ASM 0x06 PIC 0x07; TI-85 STRNG 0x0C PRGM 0x12 PICT 0x11; TI-89/92 ASM 0x21 PRGM 0x12 PIC 0x10.

devices.name: TI-83 / TI-83+ / TI-84+
devices.prefix_note: BB 6D = AsmPrgm token; required for a TI-83+/84+ program to run as machine code.
devices.note: Most documented target. 96x64, 768-byte gbuf, OS runs AsmPrgm programs directly.

devices.name: TI-85
devices.prefix_note: TI-85 has no OS asm hook; assembly ships as a string and is launched by a ZShell-compatible shell (ZShell, Usgard, Rigel). Use --type-id 18 with --ext 85p for a program variable instead.
devices.note: TI-85 ASM programs are conventionally stored as strings (see the TI Calculator FAQ).

devices.name: TI-89 / TI-89 Titanium
devices.prefix_note: Payload must be a linked AMS program (TIGCC/GCC4TI or a68k+mlink); this packer only writes the container.
devices.note: TIGCC produces .89z directly; this entry is for the packer fallback path.

devices.name: TI-90 (unshipped Z80 alias of the TI-83 class)
devices.prefix_note: Same AsmPrgm container as the TI-83 build; kept as a distinct profile so a device-specific seed and name can be used.
devices.note: No TI-90 was ever shipped. Built as a TI-83-class Z80 profile (96x64) with its own device id, seed and variable name.

devices.name: TI-92 / TI-92 Plus
devices.prefix_note: Payload must be a linked AMS program from TIGCC/GCC4TI.
devices.note: Largest LCD in the family: 240x128, 30 bytes per row, 3840-byte framebuffer.
